title: Vector Atom Model
short_intro: The vector atom model extends Bohr's semiclassical theory by incorporating spatial quantization and electron spin through angular momentum vectors. It provides a comprehensive framework to describe multi-electron atoms and accounts for fine structure and magnetic interactions.

exam_scope.tgt_core: Qualitative understanding of spatial quantization, orbital and spin magnetic moments, and basic quantum numbers for single-electron systems.
exam_scope.pgt_extension: Detailed treatment of space quantization, coupling schemes (L-S and j-j coupling), Lande g-factor, and vector addition of angular momenta in multi-electron systems.

prerequisites: Electron spin and spin quantum number

concept_notes.heading: Spatial Quantization
bullets: In the vector atom model, orbital angular momentum vector L is quantized in magnitude as sqrt(l(l+1)) ℏ.
The component of L along an external magnetic field (z-axis) is also quantized: L<sub>z</sub> = m<sub>l</sub> ℏ, where m<sub>l</sub> takes values from -l to +l.
This restriction of orientations relative to a reference axis is known as spatial quantization.

concept_notes.heading: Electron Spin and Spin-Orbit Interaction
bullets: The electron possesses an intrinsic spin angular momentum S with magnitude sqrt(s(s+1)) ℏ, where s = 1/2.
The spin component along the z-axis is S<sub>z</sub> = m<sub>s</sub> ℏ, with m<sub>s</sub> = ±1/2.
Spin-orbit interaction arises from the interaction between the magnetic moment due to electron spin and the magnetic field experienced by the electron due to its orbital motion around the nucleus.

concept_notes.heading: L-S Coupling (Russell-Saunders Coupling)
bullets: Valid for lighter atoms where electrostatic and spin-orbit interactions are dominant.
Individual orbital angular momenta l<sub>i</sub> couple to form a resultant total orbital angular momentum L = ∑ l<sub>i</sub>.
Individual spin angular momenta s<sub>i</sub> couple to form a resultant total spin angular momentum S = ∑ s<sub>i</sub>. L and S then couple to form total angular momentum J = L + S.

concept_notes.heading: j-j Coupling
bullets: Valid for heavier atoms where individual spin-orbit coupling for each electron is stronger than the electrostatic interaction between electrons.
For each electron, the orbital angular momentum l<sub>i</sub> and spin angular momentum s<sub>i</sub> couple to form individual total angular momentum j<sub>i</sub> = l<sub>i</sub> + s<sub>i</sub>.
The individual j<sub>i</sub> vectors then couple to form the total angular momentum of the atom J = ∑ j<sub>i</sub>.

derivations.title: Magnitude of Total Angular Momentum Vector
derivations.conditions: Single electron system or total resultant vector
steps: Express the angular momentum operator or vector magnitude equation: J = sqrt(j(j+1)) ℏ.
Consider the components along a chosen z-axis: J<sub>z</sub> = m<sub>j</sub> ℏ.
Apply the condition that the maximum projection of J on the z-axis cannot exceed its total magnitude, which intrinsically yields the quantum mechanical bounds for j and m<sub>j</sub>.

derivations.title: Magnetic Interaction Energy in Spin-Orbit Coupling
steps: Write the interaction energy as ΔE = A (L ⋅ S), where A is the spin-orbit coupling parameter.
Express the dot product using the resultant vector J = L + S, so that J<sup>2</sup> = L<sup>2</sup> + S<sup>2</sup> + 2(L ⋅ S).
Substitute the quantum mechanical eigenvalues for L<sup>2</sup>, S<sup>2</sup>, and J<sup>2</sup> to solve for the dot product and evaluate ΔE.

solved_numericals.question: Calculate the magnitude of orbital angular momentum of an electron in a d-state (l = 2).
solution_steps: Identify the orbital quantum number: l = 2.
Use the formula for orbital angular momentum: L = sqrt(l(l+1)) ℏ.

solved_numericals.question: Find the possible values of the total angular momentum quantum number j for an electron in a p-state (l = 1) where spin s = 1/2.
solution_steps: Identify the given quantum numbers: l = 1, s = 1/2.
Determine the range of j using the relation j = |l - s| to (l + s) in integer steps.

solved_numericals.question: Calculate the Lande g-factor for an atomic state with quantum numbers l = 1, s = 1/2, and j = 3/2.
solution_steps: Recall the formula for Lande g-factor: g = 1 + [j(j+1) + s(s+1) - l(l+1)] / [2j(j+1)].

assumptions_and_limitations: Assumption: Electrons can be treated as having well-defined classical-like angular momentum vectors that obey quantum mechanical commutation rules.
Limitation: Fails to fully account for relativistic quantum electrodynamic effects in very heavy, highly ionized atoms without Dirac equation corrections.

common_misconceptions.wrong: The angular momentum vector L can point in any arbitrary direction in space.
common_misconceptions.correct: L is spatially quantized and can only take orientations such that its z-component is an integer multiple of ℏ.
common_misconceptions.why: Quantum mechanics restricts the simultaneous measurement of the magnitude and components of angular momentum.

common_misconceptions.wrong: In j-j coupling, individual orbital and spin momenta are independent of each other.
common_misconceptions.correct: In j-j coupling, the spin and orbital momenta of the same electron strongly couple first to form j<sub>i</sub>.
common_misconceptions.why: Spin-orbit interaction for individual electrons dominates over electrostatic repulsion between different electrons in heavy atoms.

quick_revision: Orbital angular momentum magnitude is given by sqrt(l(l+1)) ℏ with z-projection m<sub>l</sub> ℏ.
Z-component of Orbital Angular Momentum: L_z = m_l \hbar
